system.title: Priest
system.biography:
Background

When you were alive, you seemed to be just one more working-class woman attending your local evangelical church. One night the survivors of a pack from a failed crusade sheltered in your basement and discovered that all on your own, you'd reinvented most of the trappings of classical infernalism. Beneath your calm exterior, you were angry enough at the world to try everything you could think of that might summon demons. The survivors consulted briefly and offered you the Embrace into the spiritual side of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}. You accepted. Now you throw yourself without reserve into the war. You want to see humanity crushed and the worthy few, yourself included, elevated to supreme power. God Himself can't hide from you forever. When you find Him, you'll pull Him down and crush him, too. In the meantime, you train yourself and your packmates to make fullest use of your blessed nature.

Roleplaying Hints

They're all going to get what's coming to them. You'll see to it. You're halfway to union with the First Rebel, the man who showed by his example how to exist free of subservience and fear. You love your condition and wish to help those around you do the same. By yourself you were nothing, but these wonderful people helped you find your way. In return, you owe them all the counsel you can provide. Alarmists say the Final Nights are here. If it's time for the consummation of the war, you'll make sure your troops go into battle blessed and ready.

system.description: You may double the range of your sight and hearing and sharpen your other senses to remarkable acuity, perceiving things ordinary folk cannot. A sudden sensory assault, such as a loud noise or strong odor, numbs the affected sense for the rest of the scene and stuns you for a turn unless you spend a Willpower Trait. You may also receive uncontrollable visions of past or future events.

Maintain physical contact with an object or location and concentrate for a turn, expending a Mental Trait, then ask the Narrator one question about who last touched it, whether it was involved in stressful situations, or what strong emotions drove its user. May be used repeatedly for greater insight; objects of powerful emotional resonance may force a derangement upon the user for the scene.

By this gift, a Toreador may penetrate the "soul" of an inanimate artwork she examines, interpreting the piece, gleaning the artist's state of mind, the relationship between artist and work, and the stages of the creative process, revealed as a series of progressively paler images looking back into the work's history. Some Toreador use this to critique or authenticate a piece; others monitor their proteges' work for unspoken rebellion or sadness, or seek the "real" story behind a letter proposing an alliance. The power does not function on "living" art still in the act of performance — a play, a song, or a story being told — since such work depends on the performer's ongoing intent rather than a fixed, finished creation.

System: The character examines the work and the number of successes determines how much she perceives: a single success yields only general feelings with no historical context; two successes offer a vague sense of the work's history; three successes reveal specific details and a fuzzy timeline; four successes grant a definite sense of the artist's emotional state and a reasonable timeline; five successes let the Toreador see the work in stages, feeling what the artist felt at every step of its creation. The difficulty rises for pieces with multiple artists or a long creation span; examining something as vast as a cathedral or castle risks leaving the Toreador a gibbering wreck from informational overload.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book One: Artisans (Toreador)

system.description: By winning a Social Challenge, you heighten or dull a victim's emotions, inflicting the Negative Mental Trait Impatient or Submissive for the rest of the scene or up to an hour.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: By watching a target for a full turn and winning a Mental Challenge, you discern their Nature; alternatively, by concentrating and spending a Mental Trait, you can become immune to surprise for the scene or hour, though losing risks becoming entranced by the patterns yourself.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: Spend eight Willpower Traits and make a Static Mental Challenge against a 12-Trait difficulty to plunge an entire city (or a 30-mile radius) into temporary mass insanity: mortals riot and rampage, vampires frenzy, and other supernatural beings suffer analogous effects until the next sunrise. Any Cainite caught in the blast radius must make a Self-control/Instincts Virtue Test against a five-Trait difficulty or instantly frenzy; once recovered, she is down three Traits resisting further frenzy triggers that night.
You gain one additional health level, functioning as an extra Healthy level on your health chart, which can be lost and healed normally.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: Once hidden from sight, you may move about at a walk and remain unnoticed, automatically becoming visible only if you speak, make loud noise, or interact with your surroundings.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines
